original.target_description: Candidate primary working-paper version: baseline set B efficiency comparisons under liability and verifiability; exact assigned comparison unresolved.

n.sample_role: Candidate Table 3 condition counts are participants; Mann-Whitney tests use matching groups of eight participants as independent observations. No assigned contrast or analytic N established.
n.exclusions: Section 4.2 reports four remaining invitees dismissed per session after required participants passed control questions; no target-specific exclusion count established.

notes: Identity assessment: supplied canonical text identifies Source URL https://docs.iza.org/dp4030.pdf, IZA Discussion Paper No. 4030, February 2009, by Uwe Dulleck, Rudolf Kerschbamer and Matthias Sutter, titled The Economics of Credence Goods: On the Role of Liability, Verifiability, Reputation and Competition. This is an author-written primary experimental working paper with full methods, results, tables and supplementary material. It matches authors and subject of the neutral reference, but is a preliminary 2009 version, not the cited 2011 AER publication: the supplied text does not establish the journal DOI or exact equivalence of versions. Journal locator p. 540 cannot be mapped directly to this working-paper pagination. No PDF was supplied. Target ambiguity: description names liability and verifiability in relation to efficiency without specifying one contrast. Table 3 (working-paper p. 38) prints baseline condition means B/N 0.18, B/L 0.84, B/V 0.16, B/LV 0.81. Its efficiency significance superscripts identify B/N versus B/L, B/N versus B/LV, B/L versus B/V, and B/V versus B/LV, each with p < 0.05 in the legend. These are candidates, not assigned statistics. No mean difference is printed in this row; none was computed. Table 3 condition participant counts are B/N 96, B/L 96, B/V 88, B/LV 80. The test unit is the matching group of 8, not an individual participant. No N was summed or derived because the target comparison is unresolved. Table 4 also provides efficiency across reputation/competition conditions; Table 6 models interaction/undertreatment/overtreatment/overcharging, not efficiency. No target selected using numeric matching or input order. Unassigned replication and narrative-success fields are placeholders.
